name: Benaiah
description: Warrior living at the time of United Monarchy

points: David set his officers: Joab over the host; Jehoshaphat the recorder; Zadok and Ahimelech the priests; Seraiah the scribe; Benaiah over the Cherethites and Pelethites; and David's sons were chief rulers.

Joab was over all the host of Israel, and Benaiah the son of Jehoiada over the Cherethites and the Pelethites. Adoram was over the tribute, Jehoshaphat the son of Ahilud was recorder, and Sheva was scribe.

Abishai the brother of Joab was chief among the thirty; he lifted up his spear against three hundred and slew them and had a name among the three, and was their captain, but he attained not unto the first three. Benaiah the son of Jehoiada did many acts: he slew two lionlike men of Moab, went down and slew a lion in the midst of a pit in time of snow, and slew a goodly Egyptian with the Egyptian's own spear after plucking it out of his hand with a staff.

note.label: 2 Samuel 23: The Last Words of David and His Mighty Men

points: Shimei is commanded to build a house in Jerusalem and dwell there, never crossing the brook Kidron on pain of death, and he agrees. After three years he goes to Gath after his runaway servants and breaks the oath, so Solomon has Benaiah put him to death, and the kingdom is established in Solomon's hand.

note.label: 1 Kings 2: The Charge to Solomon and the Kingdom Established

points: Benaiah the son of Jehoiada, a valiant man of many acts, slew two lionlike men of Moab, went down and slew a lion in a pit on a snowy day, and killed an Egyptian five cubits high.
